analysis.title: Galaxy Digital Inc. (GLXY) 3Q26: Healthy operating trends, vs. a more challenging data center financing backdrop
key_insights: GLXY reported 3Q26 diluted EPS of $0.83 vs GSe $0.54 and Visible Alpha consensus $0.18. Core adj. EPS (ex-SBC, normalized tax rate) was $0.74 vs GSe $0.58 and consensus $0.26. Revenue rose 87% and adjusted expenses rose 32%.

Management is incrementally constructive on contracting the 830MW Helios Phase II data center to an investment-grade counterparty, after cancelling late-stage negotiations during the summer. Helios II remains uncontracted.

Data center financing conditions have become harder in recent weeks on a tougher macro and regulatory backdrop. Management said credit markets are close to peak nervousness, which could raise near-term funding costs.
GLXY says it does not need incremental debt financing until 1Q-2Q27. It has $4.9bn of cash and equivalents (including UST bills) against $6.3bn of non-current debt at quarter end.
Project-level financing for Helios I, Phase III construction is expected to be raised in 1H27. The company also does not need to refinance its ~$445mn of exchangeable notes maturing December 2026.
GLXY repurchased ~$79mn of stock in 3Q26 and replenished its $200mn authorization. Management intends to repurchase opportunistically.

GS raises 2026E/27E/28E Digital assets net revenue by 5%, cuts 2027E/28E Data centers revenue by 1% and cuts 2026E Treasury and Corporate revenue by 12%. Total revenue estimates change by -2%/+1%/+1%.

Global markets net revenue was $53mn, up 8% QoQ and 18% above GSe. Trading volumes rose 12% QoQ and the average loan book rose 27% sequentially on early traction from the Galaxy On Chain Financing Rate (GOFR). GS raises 2026E/27E/28E Global markets revenue by 8%/9%/8%.
Management expects to shift toward more recurring revenue as it scales digital asset infrastructure offerings, including a recent partnership with BNY.

Asset management net revenue was $19mn, up 11% QoQ and 4% below GSe. End-of-period AUM rose 35% QoQ on higher digital asset prices and $160mn+ of net inflows, including the Galaxy Sharplink Onchain Yield Fund launch. Assets under stake rose 64% QoQ. GS cuts 2026E/27E/28E Asset management revenue by 4%/7%/4%.
The first close of Galaxy Digital Ventures Fund II is expected in late 4Q26, with a target fund size of ~$250-300mn.

Data center net revenue was $79mn, in line with GSe, with adj. EBITDA of $69mn. This was the first full quarter of lease revenue from Helios I, Phase I. Helios I, Phase II construction remains on schedule for 2Q27 data halls.

Caspian, an expansion data center site, received a studied-load classification from ERCOT's Batch Zero process rather than the expected base-load classification. This could delay development pending ERCOT's restudy in April 2027.
GLXY contracts directly with CRWV's parent company, giving it exposure to the whole CRWV customer base rather than single site-level counterparty risk.

Adjusted operating margin of 58.2% was in line with GSe and 17.5pp above consensus. Adj. operating expenses (ex-SBC) of $238mn were 20% above GSe and 32% above consensus, driven by ~105% higher interest expense and G&A vs the Street. GS raises 2026E/27E/28E adj. opex by 12%/3%/3%.

GS cuts its 12-month price target to $20.50 from $24.00 and keeps a Neutral rating. Its SOTP uses 14.5x EV/adj. EBITDA for Data centers (from 13.5x), 23.5x P/E for Digital assets and 1.0x P/TBV for Treasury.

market_movers.rationale: GS cut its target to $20.50 from $24.00 and kept Neutral. It cites updated management commentary, a roll-forward of target multiples and a modestly weaker crypto backdrop quarter to date. The stock is at $15.68, implying 30.7% upside.

earnings_insights: GLXY 3Q26 diluted EPS reported $0.83 vs GSe $0.54 and Visible Alpha consensus $0.18, all reported on 10/27/2026 for the quarter.
GLXY 3Q26 core adj. EPS (ex-SBC, normalized tax rate) was $0.74 reported vs GSe $0.58 and consensus $0.26.
3Q26 revenue rose 87% (period basis not specified) and adjusted expenses rose 32%.
GS adj. EPS (ex-SBC) estimates for 2026E/27E/28E are now $0.07/-$0.29/$0.06 (GS estimates, from $0.04/-$0.26/$0.12).
Segment results vs GSe: Global markets net revenue $53mn (18% above), Asset management $19mn (4% below), Data centers $79mn (in line) with adj. EBITDA $69mn.
crypto_views: Galaxy's 3Q26 digital asset activity was strong: trading volumes rose 12% QoQ and the average loan book rose 27% QoQ.
Digital asset prices were higher over 3Q26 but weaker quarter to date in 4Q26, which GS reflects in lower Asset management revenue estimates.
Assets under stake rose 64% QoQ on higher digital asset prices and flows from ETF providers delegating staking to GLXY.
Galaxy launched the Galaxy Sharplink Onchain Yield Fund, an institutional fund deploying capital across DeFi liquidity protocols to generate yield.
GS lists favorable crypto regulation, higher crypto market cap and faster institutional uptake of digital assets as upside risks.
risk_factors: Crypto market volatility and a persistently lower crypto market cap.
Slowing AI investment and data center oversupply.
Tighter data center financing, with higher funding costs for Helios I, Phase III project financing expected in 1H27.
Possible Caspian delay pending ERCOT's restudy in April 2027.

tension_points.bull_case: GLXY has $4.9bn of cash and equivalents and needs no incremental debt financing until 1Q-2Q27. It is also incrementally constructive on contracting Helios II to an investment-grade tenant.
tension_points.bear_case: Data center financing conditions have worsened on macro and regulatory scrutiny, with credit markets near peak nervousness. Helios II is uncontracted, and project-level financing for Helios I, Phase III in 1H27 could cost more.
tension_points.what_invalidates: An inability to contract Helios II with an investment-grade tenant, or sharply higher project financing costs when Helios I, Phase III financing is raised in 1H27.

theme_stances.key_argument: Regulatory and market scrutiny of data centers and nervous credit markets could raise GLXY's funding costs.
